title: Routing and Request Handling
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of routing and request handling using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates routing and request handling.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Routing and Request Handling** as part of **Kotlin for Backend and Server-Side Development**. A server endpoint should validate input, apply authorization at the server boundary, return consistent status codes, and be covered by tests and operational monitoring. Use the subtopics—Defining Routes, Reading Parameters and Request Bodies, Returning Structured Responses—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Backend code handles untrusted requests and persistent data. Validation, authorization, predictable errors, and operational checks must happen on the server.
